passages.title: Agricultural productivity and ecological strain
passages.body:
Directions: Read the following passage carefully and answer the items that follow the passage. Your answers to these items should be based solely on the passage.

Can agricultural productivity meet human needs in the long run? Since twentieth century advances, given increasing costs, do not seem sustainable, further increases in output will not be achieved easily. Global population growth, while showing signs of slowing down, has pushed farmers and herders into areas unsuited to intensive agriculture, accelerating worldwide ecological disruptions. Reserves of arable land and fresh water have diminished alarmingly. Chemical runoffs have compounded pollution problems. Invasion of natural habitats have hastened species extinction. Desertification has been severe in the last hundred years, especially in North Africa, southern portions of Africa, Australia, northern Mexico, and the American Southwest. Tropical forests have shrunk by one-half since World War II, with agricultural pressures causing three-quarters of that loss. Government intervention has produced its share of catastrophes, ranging from a terrible famine in China between 1958-1961 that may have killed 30 million people and destroyed the Aral Sea. Taking everything into consideration, we may remain hopeful about humankind's agricultural prospects, but we can scarcely look forward optimistically at the end of the first quarter of the twenty-first century.
passages.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part A English

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.topic: Active and Passive Voice / Direct and Indirect Speech
questions.question:
Directions: The following item has a sentence in direct speech, followed by four options. One of the options correctly converts the direct speech into indirect speech. Select the most appropriate option.

Convert from direct into indirect speech.

Ayushi said to the group, "We have had enough of suffering today. It is time to march forward."
questions.opt_a: Ayushi told the group that they had had enough of suffering that day and it was time to march forward
questions.opt_b: Ayushi asked the group that they had had enough of suffering this day and it was time to march forward
questions.opt_c: Ayushi told the group that they had enough of suffering and that it is time to march forward
questions.opt_d: Ayushi told the group that we had had enough of suffering this day and it was time to march forward
questions.explanation:
In reported speech: 'said to' becomes 'told', 'we' becomes 'they', 'have had' becomes 'had had', 'today' becomes 'that day', and 'is' becomes 'was'. Only (a) makes all these changes.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part A English

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.topic: Active and Passive Voice / Direct and Indirect Speech
questions.question:
Directions: The following item has a sentence in direct speech, followed by four options. One of the options correctly converts the direct speech into indirect speech. Select the most appropriate option.

Convert from direct speech into indirect speech.

"Alas! We lost the match by one point," said the Captain
questions.opt_a: The Captain regretted that they had lost the match by one point
questions.opt_b: The Captain regretted that they lost the match by one point
questions.opt_c: The Captain exclaimed that they had lost the match by one point
questions.opt_d: The Captain told the team that they had lost the match by one point
questions.explanation:
'Alas!' expresses sorrow, so the reporting verb should show regret, and the simple past 'lost' shifts to the past perfect 'had lost'. (a) does both. (c) uses 'exclaimed' without the sense of regret.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part A English

Directions: The following item has a sentence in direct speech, followed by four options. One of the options correctly converts the direct speech into indirect speech. Select the most appropriate option.

Convert from direct speech into indirect speech.

"Where were you last week?" Alok asked Sheela
questions.opt_a: Alok told Sheela where she had been the week before
questions.opt_b: Alok asked Sheela where she had been the week before
questions.opt_c: Alok asked Sheela where she was the week before
questions.opt_d: Alok asked Sheela where she had been the last week
questions.explanation:
A question keeps 'asked'; 'were' shifts to 'had been'; 'last week' becomes 'the week before'.
Answer: (b)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.topic: Active and Passive Voice / Direct and Indirect Speech
questions.question:
Directions: The following item has a sentence in active voice with four options. One of the options converts the active voice into passive voice correctly. Select the most appropriate option.

The king who the people loved built the castle five centuries ago
questions.opt_a: The castle was built five centuries ago by the king who was loved by the people
questions.opt_b: The castle was built five centuries ago by the king who loved the people
questions.opt_c: The castle built five centuries ago by the king loved by the people
questions.opt_d: The castle was built five centuries ago by the people who were loved by the king
questions.explanation:
Both clauses become passive: 'the castle was built ... by the king' and 'who was loved by the people'. (b) and (d) reverse who loved whom; (c) has no finite verb.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part A English

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.topic: Active and Passive Voice / Direct and Indirect Speech
questions.question:
Directions: The following item has a sentence in active voice with four options. One of the options converts the active voice into passive voice correctly. Select the most appropriate option.

The company has recruited four hundred engineers who will have to complete an internship for three weeks
questions.opt_a: Four hundred engineers have been recruited by the company and an internship of three weeks will have to be completed by them
questions.opt_b: Four hundred engineers have been recruited by the company and they will have to complete an internship of three weeks
questions.opt_c: The company has been recruited by four hundred engineers and an internship of three week will have to be completed by them
questions.opt_d: Four hundred engineers have been recruited by the company. Internship of three weeks will have had to be completed by them
questions.explanation:
Both active verbs must become passive: 'have been recruited by the company' and 'will have to be completed by them'. (b) leaves the second clause active; (c) reverses the agent; (d) changes the tense.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part A English

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: In the following item, a pair of words is provided. Select the option that most appropriately describes the meaning of both the words.

Seldom and Often
questions.opt_a: Seldom means hardly ever and often means time and again
questions.opt_b: Seldom means time and again and often means hardly ever
questions.opt_c: Seldom means never and often means not at all
questions.opt_d: Seldom means frequently and often means time and again
questions.explanation:
Seldom means rarely (hardly ever); often means frequently (time and again).
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part A English

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: In the following item, a pair of words is provided. Select the option that most appropriately describes the meaning of both the words.

Overview and Review
questions.opt_a: Overview means assessment and review means general idea
questions.opt_b: Overview means general idea and review means assessment
questions.opt_c: Overview means general analysis and review means go through
questions.opt_d: Overview means summary and review means evaluation

An overview gives a general idea of something; a review is a careful assessment of it. (b) states both correctly.
Answer: (b)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: In the following item, a pair of words is provided. Select the option that most appropriately describes the meaning of both the words.

Overcome and Succeed
questions.opt_a: Overcome means triumph over and succeed means to achieve something
questions.opt_b: Overcome means achieve something and succeed means to triumph over
questions.opt_c: Overcome means to be successful and succeed means to achieve something
questions.opt_d: Overcome means winning and succeed means to rise above
questions.explanation:
To overcome is to triumph over a difficulty; to succeed is to achieve what one aimed for.
Answer: (a)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: In the following item, a pair of words is provided. Select the option that most appropriately describes the meaning of both the words.

Embed and Imbue
questions.opt_a: Embed means instil and imbue means implant
questions.opt_b: Embed means implant and imbue means instil
questions.opt_c: Embed means accept and imbue means detest
questions.opt_d: Embed means include and imbue means accept
questions.explanation:
To embed is to fix firmly inside something (implant); to imbue is to fill or inspire with a quality (instil).
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part A English

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:

Emancipate and Empower

questions.opt_b: Emancipate means liberate and empower means authorise
questions.opt_c: Emancipate means liberal and empower means authorisation
questions.opt_d: Emancipate means freedom and empower means encounter

The Professor has been able to __instil__ confidence in her students

The members of the group expressed their __allegiance__ to their leader

The __inscrutability__ surrounding the incident remains unresolved until the end of the movie

Inscrutability is the quality of being impossible to understand, i.e. mystery. (a) and (b) are opposites.

The __dodgy__ behaviour of the leader led to her fall
questions.explanation:
'Dodgy' means dishonest or unreliable. Behaviour that brings about a leader's fall is best read as dishonest; 'dubious' (doubtful) is weaker.
Answer: (c)

People have been advised not to venture into sea as the weather is likely to be __inclement__
questions.explanation:
Inclement weather is cold, wet and stormy; 'squally' (marked by sudden storms) is closest. 'Indigent' means poor.

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: The item consists of six sentences of a passage. The first and sixth sentences are given in the beginning as S1 and S6. The middle four sentences have been jumbled up and labelled as P, Q, R and S. Find the proper sequence of the four sentences.

S1. Sufism is an English word coined in the Nineteenth Century
S6. It may also have been suffa, the platform outside a place of Islamic worship
P. Historians have understood this term in several ways
Q. According to some scholars, it is derived from suf, meaning wool
R. Others derive it from safa, meaning purity
S. The word used for Sufism in Islamic texts is tasawwuf
questions.explanation:
S1 introduces the English word; S gives the Islamic term, tasawwuf; P says historians understand 'this term' in several ways; Q and R give two derivations ('some scholars', 'Others'); S6 adds a third ('It may also have been').
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part A English

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: The item consists of six sentences of a passage. The first and sixth sentences are given in the beginning as S1 and S6. The middle four sentences have been jumbled up and labelled as P, Q, R and S. Find the proper sequence of the four sentences.

S1. Al-Biruni was born in 973, in Khwarizm in present-day Uzbekistan
S6. He arrived in Ghazni as a hostage, but gradually developed a liking for the city
P. In 1017, when Sultan Mahmud invaded Khwarizm, he took several scholars back to his capital, Ghazni: Al-Biruni was one among them
Q. He was well versed in several languages; Syriac, Arabic, Persian, Hebrew, and Sanskrit
R. Khwarizm was an important centre of learning, and Al-Biruni received the best education available at the time
S. However he did not know Greek, although he was familiar with the works of Plato and other Greek philosophers
questions.explanation:
R follows the birthplace with his education there; Q lists his languages and S qualifies that ('However he did not know Greek'); P describes his removal to Ghazni, which leads into S6 ('arrived in Ghazni as a hostage').
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part A English

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: The item consists of six sentences of a passage. The first and sixth sentences are given in the beginning as S1 and S6. The middle four sentences have been jumbled up and labelled as P, Q, R and S. Find the proper sequence of the four sentences.

S1. Vijayanagara or 'city of victory' was the name of both a city and an empire
S6. They remembered it as Hampi, a name derived from that of the local mother goddess, Pampadevi
P. In its heyday it stretched from the river Krishna in the north to the extreme south of the Indian peninsula
Q. Although it fell into ruin in the seventeenth-eighteenth centuries, it continued to live in the memories of the people who inhabited the Krishna-Tungabhadra doab
R. In 1565 the city was sacked and subsequently deserted
S. The Empire was founded in the fourteenth century
questions.explanation:
The story runs in time order: founding (S), its greatest extent (P), the sack of 1565 (R), and its survival in memory (Q), which leads into S6 ('They remembered it as Hampi').
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part A English

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: The item consists of six sentences of a passage. The first and sixth sentences are given in the beginning as S1 and S6. The middle four sentences have been jumbled up and labelled as P, Q, R and S. Find the proper sequence of the four sentences.

S1. Liberalisation and globalisation freed India's economy from the low GDP trap that had impeded India's progress
S6. Today India has transformed into one of the largest economies of the world
P. India's 3 pc rate of growth and a set of emergent circumstances led to a balance of payment crisis in the early 1990s
Q. Ease of business was ensured, and the requirement for import licences, and production quotas, were removed
R. Apart from these measures India also took a loan from the IMF to tide over the crisis, but after 1993, India has not taken another loan from the IMF
S. In a landmark budget in 1991, responding to the emergent crisis, India delicenced many industries and liberalised its economic policies
questions.explanation:
P describes the crisis; S gives the 1991 response; Q lists more reforms; R ('Apart from these measures') adds the IMF loan; S6 states the result.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part A English

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.topic: Ordering of Sentences in a Passage
questions.question:
Directions: The item consists of six sentences of a passage. The first and sixth sentences are given in the beginning as S1 and S6. The middle four sentences have been jumbled up and labelled as P, Q, R and S. Find the proper sequence of the four sentences.

S1. In many countries, there are millions of people who are underprivileged and deprived
S6. In the past forced labour was imposed by landlords, money-lenders, and other wealthy persons
P. Both of these are prohibited under the Constitution of India
Q. One such form of exploitation in our country has been begar or forced labour without payment
R. The marginalised are often subjected to exploitation by their fellow human beings
S. Another closely related form of exploitation is buying and selling of human beings and using them as slaves
questions.explanation:
R introduces exploitation; Q gives 'one such form' (begar); S gives 'another closely related form'; P says 'Both of these' are prohibited; S6 returns to forced labour in the past.
Answer: (b)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: The sentence uses a discourse marker/expression to make it complete. Identify the most appropriate discourse marker.

I can't be bothered to tell him what I think; __________ he would not listen to me.
questions.explanation:
'In any case' adds a further reason that makes the first point unimportant: telling him is pointless because he would not listen anyway.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part A English

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: The sentence uses a discourse marker/expression to make it complete. Identify the most appropriate discourse marker.

__________, if the referee points his fingers, this indicates that someone has done something wrong.
questions.explanation:
The sentence states a rule in a short, summary form. 'Briefly' introduces such a short statement. 'On the contrary' needs a contrast, 'Whatever more' is not idiomatic and 'As regards' needs a noun after it.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part A English

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: The sentence uses a discourse marker/expression to make it complete. Identify the most appropriate discourse marker.

__________, have you been to the local library yet?
questions.explanation:
'Incidentally' introduces a new topic or a passing question.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part A English

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: The sentence uses a discourse marker/expression to make it complete. Identify the most appropriate discourse marker.

__________, women are healthier and are living longer than ever before: indeed on an average, they can expect to live five years longer than men.
questions.explanation:
'To a large extent' qualifies a general claim. 'As regards' and 'As far as' need a following noun or clause.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part A English

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: The sentence uses a discourse marker/expression to make it complete. Identify the most appropriate discourse marker.

The difference is that I have been fortunate to find a career that I love and, __________, I am getting paid reasonably for it.
questions.explanation:
'What is more' adds a further, stronger point.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part A English

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: The sentence uses a discourse marker/expression to make it complete. Identify the most appropriate discourse marker.

__________, the Government of India has followed the policy of trying to improve relations with its neighbours.
questions.explanation:
'In general' introduces a broad statement about a usual policy. 'Particular' is an adjective and does not fit here.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part A English

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: The sentence uses a discourse marker/expression to make it complete. Identify the most appropriate discourse marker.

__________, this issue is likely to be discussed when the Council meets next.
questions.explanation:
The sentence reports an expectation that comes from other sources, so 'As per reports' fits. Nothing earlier makes 'Accordingly' or 'Likewise' appropriate.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part A English

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: The sentence uses a discourse marker/expression to make it complete. Identify the most appropriate discourse marker.

__________, you needed to consult a physician to have a clear idea of what the disease is about.
questions.explanation:

Corollary:

A quandary is a state of uncertainty about what to do.
Answer: (a)

Presumption:

Answer: (d)

Smug:

questions.opt_d: Too eager to bottle up conflicts

S: that underscores the learning process and contributes

That sporting activities are an integral part (Q) of school education is an ineluctable truth (P) that underscores the learning process and contributes (S) meaningfully towards the overall growth of a student (R).
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part A English

questions.question:

R: well without retribution or rebuke
S: a virtuous life is peace of mind
questions.explanation:
The beneficial outcome of (Q) a virtuous life is peace of mind (S) and contentment on account of a life lived (P) well without retribution or rebuke (R).
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part A English

questions.question:

P: more representative than the latter

R: in as much as the former is
S: it is widely believed that the parliamentary system differs
questions.explanation:
It is widely believed that the parliamentary system differs (S) from a non-parliamentary system (Q) in as much as the former is (R) more representative than the latter (P).
Answer: (a)

S: when service is done for

When service is done for (S) exhibition or for fear of public opinion (R), it stunts the person offering the same and (Q) crushes the spirit behind the service (P).
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part A English

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: The sentence has a blank space, followed by four options. Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

It does not look like he is going __________ in his studies than what was predicted by his school principal.
questions.explanation:
'Further' is used for figurative progress (farther is for physical distance). In a negative sentence 'any further' is idiomatic: 'not going any further'.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part A English

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: The sentence has a blank space, followed by four options. Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

__________ all the confusion the thief made a quiet getaway.
questions.explanation:
'Among/amongst' are used with countable plurals; 'confusion' is uncountable, so 'amid' (in the middle of) is required. 'Amidst' is an older, more literary form of the same word.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part A English

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: The sentence has a blank space, followed by four options. Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The intricate operation on the patient required the expertise of a/an __________ surgeon.
questions.explanation:
'Specialist surgeon' is the standard term for a surgeon with expert training in one field. 'Special' and 'especial' mean unusual or particular.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part A English

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question:
Directions: The sentence has a blank space, followed by four options. Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

There are __________ thirty students inside the classroom at any time.
questions.explanation:
'Fewer' is used with countable nouns such as students, and the comparison word is 'than', not 'then'.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part A English

questions.question:
Directions: The sentence has a blank space, followed by four options. Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

There are many __________ vehicles on the highway due to a sudden landslide.
questions.explanation:
Vehicles unable to move because of a landslide are 'stranded'. 'Stationery' means writing materials.
Answer: (c)

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: The focal length of a concave lens is 0.5 m. The power of the lens is
questions.explanation:
Concept: $P=1/f$ (in metres), and a concave lens has a negative focal length.
Step 1: $P=\dfrac{1}{-0.5}=-2.0$ D.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: The rule to determine the direction of a force experienced by a straight current carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field which is perpendicular to it is
questions.explanation:
Fleming's left-hand rule gives the direction of force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field (motor rule). The right-hand rule gives the induced current (generator rule).
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: One parsec in astronomical units (A.U.) is about
questions.explanation:
1 parsec is the distance at which 1 AU subtends 1 arc-second: $1\text{ pc}=\dfrac{1}{\tan 1''}\text{ AU}\approx206265\text{ AU}\approx2\times10^5$ AU.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements for second law of motion is NOT correct?
questions.opt_a: The net force on a body is proportional to that body's acceleration
questions.opt_b: The net force on a body is in the same direction as the acceleration
questions.opt_c: The time rate of change of momentum is equal to force
questions.opt_d: The net force on a body is proportional to that body's momentum
questions.explanation:
Newton's second law: $F=\dfrac{dp}{dt}=ma$. Force is proportional to the rate of change of momentum, not to momentum itself.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: The temperature of a body increases from 310 K to 340 K. The temperature increase in degree Celsius is
questions.explanation:
A change of 1 K equals a change of 1°C, so a rise of $340-310=30$ K is a rise of 30°C.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.theme: Work done by a conservative force
questions.question: Which one of the following statements for the work done by gravity on a body is NOT correct?
questions.opt_a: Work done is independent of the path followed by the body
questions.opt_b: Work done depends only on the vertical distance separating the initial and the final position of the body
questions.opt_c: Work done depends on the path followed by the body
questions.opt_d: Work done is zero if the body is displaced horizontally to the force of gravity
questions.explanation:
Gravity is a conservative force: its work depends only on the change in height, not on the path. So (c) is the incorrect statement.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Which one among the following statements is correct?
questions.opt_a: Pressure has magnitude as well as direction
questions.opt_b: As we go deeper in a liquid, the pressure decreases
questions.opt_c: Action and reaction forces act on the same object
questions.opt_d: Pascal and N/m$^{2}$ represent the same unit
questions.explanation:
Pressure is a scalar; it increases with depth; action and reaction act on different bodies. 1 Pa is defined as 1 N/m$^2$.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Which one of the following wavelength radiations may correspond to an X-ray?
questions.explanation:
X-rays span roughly 0.01 nm to 10 nm, with typical values around 0.1-1 nm. 100 nm and 300 nm are ultraviolet, and 10 nm is at the UV/X-ray boundary. 1 nm is clearly an X-ray.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: In a Telescope, compared to the eyepiece lens the objective lens has
questions.opt_a: larger focal length and larger aperture
questions.opt_b: larger focal length and smaller aperture
questions.opt_c: smaller focal length and larger aperture
questions.opt_d: smaller focal length and smaller aperture
questions.explanation:
A telescope objective has a long focal length (for magnification $f_o/f_e$) and a large aperture to gather light.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: The energy, $E$, of a photon can be expressed as $E=hf$ where $f$ is the frequency and $h$ is Planck's constant. The dimensions of $h$ are the same as that of
questions.explanation:
$h=E/f$ has units J s $=$ kg m$^2$ s$^{-1}$, which are the units of angular momentum ($mvr$).
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.question: The work done by the force acting on an object is zero if the displacement of the object
questions.opt_a: is in the opposite direction of the direction of force
questions.opt_b: is in the same direction of the direction of force
questions.opt_c: is in perpendicular direction of the direction of force
questions.explanation:
$W=Fd\cos\theta$ is zero when $\theta=90^\circ$.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: The magnetic field inside a current carrying very long solenoid is
questions.explanation:
Inside a long solenoid the field lines are parallel and evenly spaced: $B=\mu_0nI$ is uniform.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Which one of the following instruments can be used to measure -250°C temperature?
questions.opt_a: By using a mercury based thermometer
questions.opt_b: By using an alcohol based thermometer
questions.explanation:
Mercury freezes at about -39°C and alcohol at about -114°C; a clinical thermometer covers only 35-42°C. Thermocouples work down to cryogenic temperatures near -270°C.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: The quantity of heat needed to change unit mass of a substance from liquid to vapour without changing the temperature, is called
questions.explanation:
Heat absorbed per unit mass during a change of state at constant temperature is the specific latent heat (here, of vaporisation).
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: The temperature at which "vapour pressure of the liquid in an open vessel becomes equal to the atmospheric pressure" is called
questions.explanation:
A liquid boils when its vapour pressure equals the surrounding pressure.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements about surface tension is correct?
questions.opt_c: It will remain same with increase or decrease of temperature
questions.opt_d: It will always decrease with increase or decrease of temperature
questions.explanation:
Rising temperature weakens intermolecular cohesion, so surface tension falls as temperature rises.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: A body sinks in water when
questions.opt_a: density of water is greater than density of body
questions.opt_b: density of water is less than density of body
questions.opt_c: density of water is equal to density of body
questions.explanation:
A body sinks when its weight exceeds the buoyant force, i.e. when its density is greater than that of water.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Why a fielder in the ground gradually pulls his hands backward while catching a fast moving cricket ball?
questions.opt_a: To reduce the acceleration of the ball
questions.opt_b: To increase the acceleration of the ball
questions.opt_c: To increase the velocity of the ball
questions.explanation:
Pulling the hands back increases the time taken to stop the ball. The same change in momentum over a longer time means a smaller deceleration and therefore a smaller force on the hands.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Bottom of a tank containing water appears to be raised. It is due to
questions.explanation:
Light from the bottom bends away from the normal as it passes from water into air, so the bottom appears at a smaller apparent depth (real depth divided by refractive index).
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: SONAR stands for
questions.explanation:
SONAR is Sound Navigation and Ranging; it uses ultrasonic echoes to locate underwater objects.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Which one of the following radiations has longer wavelength?
questions.explanation:
In order of increasing wavelength: X-rays < ultraviolet < infrared < microwaves.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: For a material under static conditions, which one among the following statements is correct?
questions.opt_b: A perfect conductor can be charged
questions.opt_c: Both perfect conductor and insulator can be charged
questions.opt_d: Both perfect conductor and insulator cannot be charged
questions.explanation:
Any isolated body can hold a static charge. An insulator keeps it where it is placed; an insulated conductor keeps it on its outer surface. So both can be charged.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: A person can see nearby objects clearly but cannot see distant object distinctly, the person is suffering with
questions.explanation:
Short-sightedness (myopia) is the inability to see distant objects clearly; it is corrected with a concave lens.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.theme: Conservation of energy in isolated systems
questions.question: The energy is always conserved for a system which is
questions.explanation:
The total energy of a system stays constant only if no energy enters or leaves it, i.e. for an isolated system. A non-isolated system can gain or lose energy.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Suppose, a ball of mass M is thrown upwards from a point A and it reaches up to the highest point B and returns back to point A, which one among the following is correct?
questions.opt_a: Kinetic Energy at A = Potential Energy at B
questions.opt_b: Kinetic Energy at A = Potential Energy at A
questions.opt_c: Kinetic Energy at B = Potential Energy at B
questions.opt_d: Kinetic Energy at B = Kinetic Energy at A
questions.explanation:
Taking A as the zero of potential energy and ignoring air resistance, all the kinetic energy at A becomes potential energy at the highest point B, where the speed is zero.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: History

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Chola inscriptions mention several categories of lands. Which one of the following was meant for the maintenance of school?

questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: History

2. Annie Besant announced the formation of Home Rule League in September 1916

questions.opt_b: Economic recovery after the Second World War
questions.opt_c: International Bank for Reconstruction and Development
questions.opt_d: Establishment of a monetary system based on floating exchange rate

Sandhyakara Nandi's Ramacharita (12th century) narrates the story of Rama and of the Pala king Ramapala at the same time, verse by verse.

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Which of the following Acts established the Board of Control to guide and control the work of the Court of Directors and the Government of India?

questions.subject: History
questions.question: Who among the following Sikh Gurus laid the foundation of the Khalsa Panth?

Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa at Anandpur in 1699.
Answer: (d)

questions.subject: Economy
questions.question: Which one among the following plans is also known as Mahalanobis Plan?

The Second Five Year Plan (1956-61), stressing heavy industry, was based on P. C. Mahalanobis's model.

questions.question: Which of the following were the years of Annual Plans?
questions.explanation:
After the Third Plan, three Annual Plans were run from 1966 to 1969 (the 'plan holiday') before the Fourth Plan. Another pair of annual plans ran in 1990-92.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about BRICS Summits:

1. The first BRICS Summit was held in Brazil
2. BRICS Summits were held in New Delhi on three occasions

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
The first (BRIC) summit was held at Yekaterinburg, Russia in 2009. India hosted in 2012 (New Delhi), 2016 (Goa) and 2021 (virtual, chaired from New Delhi), so only one in-person summit was held in New Delhi.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: History
questions.question:
Placing the earliest first, arrange the following international events in the chronological order:

1. Introduction of www (World Wide Web)
2. Advent of Inter-Continental Ballistic Missiles
3. Launch of first communication satellite

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
The first ICBM (Soviet R-7) flew in 1957; the first communication satellite (SCORE, 1958; Telstar, 1962) followed; the World Wide Web came in 1989-91.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question:
Which of the following rights under the Constitution of India is/are Fundamental Right(s)?

1. Right to work
2. Right to privacy
3. Right to free and compulsory education in the age bracket of six to eighteen years

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
The right to work is a Directive Principle (Article 41). Privacy is part of Article 21 (Puttaswamy, 2017). Article 21A covers children aged 6 to 14, not 6 to 18.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.question:
Consider the following statements with regard to flags of International Organizations:

1. The flag of EU has a circle of gold stars on a white background
2. The Flag of the UN carries two pairs of olive tree branches
3. The ASEAN flag carries blue, red, white and yellow colours

How many of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
The EU flag has 12 gold stars on a blue background. The UN flag shows the world map within a wreath of two olive branches (one pair). The ASEAN flag uses blue, red, white and yellow. Only 3 is correct.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Polity
questions.question: Which one of the following committees is NOT associated with decentralization of Panchayati Raj institutions in India?
questions.explanation:
Balwant Rai Mehta (1957), Ashok Mehta (1977) and L. M. Singhvi (1986) all dealt with Panchayati Raj. The Abhijit Sen Committee (2000-02) dealt with long-term grain policy.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: The reaction that occurs on passing carbon dioxide gas through lime water is
questions.explanation:
Lime water is calcium hydroxide solution; CO$_2$ forms insoluble calcium carbonate, which makes it milky. (a) happens only with excess CO$_2$.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.subtopic: Acids, Bases, pH & Commercial Inorganic Salts
questions.question: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
questions.opt_a: Water of crystallization is the fixed number of water molecules present in one formula unit of a salt
questions.opt_b: The molecular formula of Plaster of Paris is $\mathrm{CaSO_4\cdot 2H_2O}$
questions.opt_c: Washing soda is used for removing the permanent hardness of water
questions.opt_d: The atmosphere of Venus is made up of thick white and yellow clouds of sulphuric acid
questions.explanation:
Plaster of Paris is $\mathrm{CaSO_4\cdot\tfrac12H_2O}$; $\mathrm{CaSO_4\cdot2H_2O}$ is gypsum.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Which one of the following type of medicines is used for treating indigestion?
questions.explanation:
Antacids neutralise excess stomach acid and relieve indigestion.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Which one of the following is NOT present in cement?
questions.explanation:
Portland cement contains dicalcium silicate, tricalcium silicate, tricalcium aluminate and tetracalcium aluminoferrite. There is no '4CaO·SiO$_2$'.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Which one of the following is NOT a chemical change?
questions.explanation:
Melting changes only the physical state of water; no new substance is formed.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
questions.opt_a: The interconversion of states of matter is a physical change
questions.opt_b: During burning of a candle, both chemical and physical changes take place
questions.opt_c: During a physical change, the chemical composition of molecules changes
questions.opt_d: Rusting of iron is a chemical change
questions.explanation:
In a physical change the composition stays the same; only the form or state changes.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Which one of the following is NOT a heterogeneous mixture?
questions.opt_b: Mixture of sugar and salt crystals
questions.explanation:
Sulphur dissolves completely in carbon disulphide and forms a uniform solution, a homogeneous mixture. Sugar and salt crystals, sand in water and sulphur in water all have visibly separate components.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question:
Match List I with List II and select the answer using the code given below the Lists:

| List I (Element) | List II (Atomicity) |
|---|---|
| A. Phosphorus | 1. 2 |
| B. Nitrogen | 2. 1 |
| C. Neon | 3. 8 |
| D. Sulphur | 4. 4 |

Code:
questions.explanation:
Phosphorus exists as P$_4$, nitrogen as N$_2$, neon as single atoms and sulphur as S$_8$.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question:
In the following redox reaction, which compound is acting as a reducing agent?

$\mathrm{N_2H_4+2H_2O_2\to N_2+4H_2O}$
questions.explanation:
Nitrogen goes from $-2$ in hydrazine to 0 in N$_2$, so hydrazine is oxidised and is the reducing agent. H$_2$O$_2$ is reduced (oxygen goes from $-1$ to $-2$).
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Which one of the following is considered to be the purest source of water?
questions.explanation:
Rain water forms by natural distillation (evaporation and condensation), so it is the purest natural water, though it can dissolve some gases.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Which one of the following salts is responsible for temporary hardness of water?
questions.explanation:
Temporary hardness is caused by bicarbonates of calcium and magnesium and is removed by boiling. Chlorides and sulphates cause permanent hardness.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question:
Match List I with List II and select the answer using the code given below the Lists:

| List I (Reaction) | List II (Type) |
|---|---|
| A. $\mathrm{CaO(s)+H_2O(l)\to Ca(OH)_2(aq)}$ | 1. Single displacement |
| B. $\mathrm{CaCO_3(s)\to CaO(s)+CO_2(g)}$ | 2. Double displacement |
| C. $\mathrm{Pb(s)+CuCl_2(aq)\to PbCl_2(aq)+Cu(s)}$ | 3. Combination |
| D. $\mathrm{Na_2SO_4(aq)+BaCl_2(aq)\to BaSO_4(s)+2NaCl(aq)}$ | 4. Decomposition |

Code:
questions.explanation:
A joins two substances (combination); B splits one (decomposition); in C lead displaces copper (single displacement); in D ions are exchanged (double displacement).
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Which one of the following is an endothermic reaction?
questions.explanation:
Combustion of methane, respiration of glucose and ammonia synthesis all release heat. Thermal decomposition of lead nitrate needs continuous heating, so it is endothermic.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Which one of the following is known as 'water gas'?
questions.explanation:
Water gas (syngas) is the mixture of carbon monoxide and hydrogen made by passing steam over red-hot coke.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
questions.opt_a: Diamond is hard due to extended covalent bonding in it
questions.opt_b: Fullerene is composed of five and six membered rings
questions.opt_c: Diamond is a good conductor of electricity
questions.opt_d: Graphite is used as a lubricant
questions.explanation:
In diamond every carbon uses all four electrons in bonds, leaving no free electrons, so diamond is a poor conductor of electricity (graphite conducts).
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Arrange the following zones in ascending order in terms of their latitudinal extent on the Earth surface:

1. Equatorial zone
2. Midlatitude zone
3. Subarctic zone
4. Tropical zone

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Using the standard latitude zones (per hemisphere): equatorial about 0-10° (10°), subarctic about 55/60-65/70° (about 10°), tropical about 10-25° (15°) and mid-latitude about 35-55° (20°). In ascending order of extent: equatorial, subarctic, tropical, mid-latitude.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Consider the following statements with reference to Feldspar mineral:

1. Half of the earth's crust is composed of feldspar
2. It has light cream to salmon pink colour
3. Magnesium is a common element in all types of feldspar

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Feldspar makes up about half of the crust and is light cream to salmon pink. Silicon and oxygen are its common elements, with sodium, potassium, calcium and aluminium; magnesium is not common to all feldspars.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Consider the following pairs with reference to sedimentary rocks and the process of their formation:

| Sedimentary Rock | Process of Formation |
|---|---|
| 1. Chert | Chemically formed |
| 2. Geyserite | Organically formed |
| 3. Shale | Mechanically formed |

Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
questions.explanation:
NCERT classifies chert as chemically formed, geyserite as organically formed and shale as mechanically formed. All three pairs are correct.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?

1. Oceanic trenches are very significant in the study of plate movements
2. Oceanic trenches are associated with active volcanoes and strong earthquakes

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Trenches mark subduction zones, so they are key evidence for plate movement, and they are associated with active volcanoes and strong earthquakes.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Which of the following statements with reference to shadow zones in an event of an earthquake is/are correct?

1. Zone between 105° and 145° from epicentre was identified as the shadow zone for both P-waves and S-waves
2. The shadow zone of P-waves is much larger than that of the S-waves

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that the zone between 105° and 145° from the epicentre is the shadow zone for both types of waves. The S-wave shadow zone (everything beyond 105°) is much larger than the P-wave shadow zone, so statement 2 is reversed.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which one among the following volcanic island chains is NOT associated with mid-oceanic ridge?
questions.explanation:
The Azores, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha lie on or near the Mid-Atlantic Ridge. The Hawaiian Islands were formed by a hotspot in the middle of the Pacific Plate.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Consider the following statements with reference to sea waves:

1. The height of waves is determined by wind speed, wind duration, and fetch
2. The energy of a wave is proportional to the square of its height
3. Waves retain most of their energy as they travel across the deep ocean

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Wave height depends on wind speed, duration and fetch; wave energy varies as the square of height; in deep water waves lose little energy until they reach shallow coasts.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Which of the following statements with reference to soil forming processes is/are correct?

1. Translocation, enrichment, removal and transformation are different classes of soil forming processes
2. In translocation, fine particles are transported downward by eluviation and accumulate in lower horizons by illuviation

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Soil-forming processes are grouped as additions (enrichment), removals, translocations and transformations. In translocation, eluviation washes fine material down and illuviation deposits it in lower horizons.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Consider the following statements with reference to structure of the Earth's atmosphere:

1. Thickness of the troposphere is greatest at the equator
2. The air temperature of the tropopause is highest above the poles
3. The temperature in troposphere decreases at the rate of 1°F for every 165 m of height

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
The troposphere is about 18 km thick at the equator and 8 km at the poles. The tropopause is about $-80$°C over the equator and about $-45$°C over the poles, so it is warmest over the poles. The lapse rate is 1°C (not 1°F) per 165 m.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Which of the following are the factors that cause variation in the amount of insolation on the Earth?

1. Rotation of the earth on its axis
2. Length of the day
3. Distribution of land and water on the earth

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
NCERT lists rotation of the earth on its axis, angle of the sun's rays, length of day, transparency of the atmosphere and the aspect of land. Land-water distribution affects how heat is absorbed and temperature, not the insolation received.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Consider the following conditions favourable for the formation and intensification of Tropical Storms:

1. Presence of the Coriolis force
2. Upper divergence above the sea level system
3. High variations in the vertical wind speed

Which of the conditions given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Tropical cyclones need warm seas, the Coriolis force, small variation in vertical wind speed (low wind shear), a pre-existing low and upper-level divergence. High vertical wind shear prevents them.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Which of the following factors influence the ocean currents?

1. Coriolis force
2. Gravity
3. Heating by solar energy
4. Wind

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Ocean currents are driven by solar heating, wind and gravity, and deflected by the Coriolis force. All four are factors.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Which of the following is/are warm ocean current(s)?

1. Alaska Current
2. Agulhas Current
3. Falkland Current
4. West Australian Current

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
The Alaska and Agulhas currents are warm; the Falkland and West Australian currents are cold.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: State of Assam shares borders with how many other countries and Indian states respectively?
questions.explanation:
Assam borders Bhutan and Bangladesh, and the states of Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, Tripura, Meghalaya and West Bengal.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which one of the following is the northernmost river basin of the Deccan Plateau?
questions.explanation:
The Chambal belongs to the Ganga system on the Malwa side and the Mahi drains the Malwa-Gujarat region. Among peninsular rivers draining the Deccan, the Narmada (in the rift valley at its northern edge) is the northernmost.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Laterite soil in India is rich in which of the following?

1. Calcium
2. Nitrogen
3. Phosphate
4. Potash

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
NCERT: laterite soils are poor in organic matter, nitrogen, phosphate and calcium, while iron oxide and potash are in excess.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Which of the following statements with reference to crops cultivated in India is/are correct?

1. Bajra grows well in sandy and shallow black soils, whereas red and shallow black soil is suited for Ragi
2. Bajra is predominantly grown in states like Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra, while Ragi is mainly cultivated in Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Himachal Pradesh

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Both match NCERT: bajra on sandy and shallow black soils in Rajasthan, UP, Maharashtra and Gujarat; ragi on red, black and shallow black soils in Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Himachal Pradesh and others.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Match List I with List II and select the answer using the code given below the Lists:

| List I (City) | List II (Mineral) |
|---|---|
| A. Bewar | 1. Manganese |
| B. Balaghat | 2. Mica |
| C. Bilaspur | 3. Iron-ore |
| D. Ballary | 4. Bauxite |

Code:
questions.explanation:
Beawar (Rajasthan) is a mica area; Balaghat (MP) is known for manganese; Bilaspur (Chhattisgarh) region for bauxite; Ballari (Karnataka) for iron ore.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which one among the following is NOT a beneficiary state from the Vindhyachal Power Plant of the NTPC?
questions.explanation:
Vindhyachal (Singrauli, MP) supplies the Western Region: Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa and the western UTs. Uttar Pradesh is in the Northern Region.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question:
Consider the following pairs with reference to Thermal Power Plants and their location in respective states in India:

| Thermal Power Plant | Located in State |
|---|---|
| I. Panki | Uttar Pradesh |
| II. Parli | Karnataka |
| III. Vijayawada | Telangana |
| IV. Vanakbari | Gujarat |

How many of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
questions.explanation:
Panki is in Kanpur (UP) and Vanakbori is in Gujarat. Parli is in Maharashtra and Vijayawada in Andhra Pradesh.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: The book 'The Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection' was authored by
questions.explanation:
Charles Darwin published On the Origin of Species in 1859.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: International Relations
questions.question: The headquarters of World Meteorological Organization (WMO) is located at
questions.explanation:
The WMO, a UN specialised agency, is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: The optimum pH at which the enzymes pepsin and trypsin of the human alimentary canal works are
questions.explanation:
Pepsin works in the acidic stomach (about pH 2); trypsin works in the alkaline small intestine (about pH 7.8-8).
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: The amount of air breathed in and out during a normal respiration by human lungs is referred to as
questions.explanation:
Tidal volume (about 500 mL) is the air inspired or expired in a normal breath.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Which one among the following statements about arteries and veins in humans is NOT correct?
questions.opt_a: Arteries carry blood away from heart while veins bring blood towards the heart
questions.opt_b: Pulmonary arteries always carry oxygenated blood while Pulmonary veins always carry deoxygenated blood
questions.opt_c: Arteries have thicker and more elastic walls compared to veins in general
questions.opt_d: Arteries do not have valves but veins do have valves
questions.explanation:
It is the reverse: the pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs and the pulmonary veins carry oxygenated blood to the heart.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Identify the functions that are controlled by the hind brain of human being
questions.opt_a: Involuntary actions such as blood pressure, salivation vomiting etc.
questions.opt_b: Controlling the regions receiving sensory impulses from receptors
questions.opt_c: Controlling the movement of voluntary muscles
questions.opt_d: Sensation of hunger or being full
questions.explanation:
The medulla in the hind brain controls involuntary actions such as blood pressure, salivation and vomiting. Sensory areas and voluntary movement belong to the forebrain (cerebrum), and hunger to the hypothalamus.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Iodized salt is a vital part of our diet as it is essential for the synthesis of
questions.explanation:
The thyroid gland needs iodine to make thyroxine; deficiency causes goitre.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.theme: Hormonal control of the menstrual cycle
questions.question: The menstrual cycle in females is controlled by hormones that are secreted by
questions.explanation:
Pituitary hormones (FSH, LH) and ovarian hormones (estrogen, progesterone) regulate the menstrual cycle.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Which one of the following blood cells type secrete large number of antibodies during an immune response of the body?
questions.explanation:
B-lymphocytes (as plasma cells) produce antibodies.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.question: Which of the following organelles have their own DNA and ribosomes?
questions.explanation:
Mitochondria and chloroplasts are semi-autonomous: they contain their own DNA and 70S ribosomes.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: What is the nickname of the National Men's Hockey Team of Australia?
questions.explanation:
Australia's men's hockey team is the Kookaburras. The Kangaroos are the rugby league team and the Boomers the men's basketball team.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: Which one of the following organisations has completed 150 years of service to the nation in the year 2025?
questions.explanation:
The India Meteorological Department was set up in 1875 and celebrated its 150th foundation year on 15 January 2025.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question:
Which of the following statements about 'Jalvahak' is/are correct?

1. It is a newly commissioned naval ship inducted into Indian Navy
2. It is a major policy for cargo promotion unveiled by the Government of India

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Jalvahak is the cargo promotion scheme launched in December 2024 to encourage cargo movement on National Waterways 1, 2 and 16. It is not a naval ship.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: How many rural districts does Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act cover as on 2024-25?
questions.explanation:
Ministry of Rural Development replies in Parliament in 2024-25 state that MGNREGS operates in 740 districts.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA II 2025 General Ability Test set A (TODC-T-GAT), Part B General Knowledge

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: Under which one of the following initiatives does the NITI Aayog support interested States to establish a State Institution for Transformation (SIT)?
questions.explanation:
Under its State Support Mission, NITI Aayog helps states set up State Institutions for Transformation to strengthen planning and policy capacity.
